__comment: Domain health — payroll, attendance, sync and workflow.
The dashboard a generic monitoring setup would never produce, because
every panel here is about what the product does rather than what a JVM
does. An infrastructure dashboard tells you a component is unhealthy;
this one tells you whether people are about to be affected — someone
not paid, a punch lost, an approval never seen.
Panels are ordered by consequence. Payroll first: a wrong or missed run
is a legal problem in every market we target, not merely an outage.
title: HR / Domain Health

list.name: tenant
list.description: Only payroll and workflow metrics carry a tenant label — see Metrics.Tag.TENANT for why. Per-tenant investigation of anything else goes through traces and logs.

panels.title: Runs failed (24h)
panels.description: Any non-zero value needs a human. Runs are resumable by phase — establish which phase failed before restarting.

panels.title: Snapshots missing
panels.description: A committed run without a retrievable input snapshot is no longer reproducible. That is a compliance problem — we could not answer 'why was I paid this?' months later. Should always be zero.

panels.title: Run duration by phase
panels.description: Budget is ten minutes for 10,000 employees. A run sitting in one phase for over an hour is wedged — most often on the Redis lock. Check the lock holder is still alive before clearing anything.

panels.title: Anomaly rate
panels.description: Results flagged against the prior period. A high rate usually means something legitimate and large happened — an annual increment, a restructure — or a pay item formula changed. Either way a human confirms before the run is approved.

panels.title: Punch ingestion by source
panels.description: Silence during working hours means ingestion is broken. Mobile clients queue locally and deliver eventually; a device-based feed may be losing data outright.

panels.title: Unprocessed punches
panels.description: daily_attendance is derived state and always recomputable, so nothing is lost — but until it catches up, employees see stale attendance and managers see an incomplete team board.

panels.title: Outbox entries lost (24h)
panels.description: Each one is a user action shown as queued that never arrived after seven days of retries. The affected users need telling; the payload is retained so it can be resubmitted.

panels.title: Forced full resyncs
panels.description: Expected for devices offline longer than the 90-day change-feed retention. A spike suggests the feed is being pruned too aggressively, or clients are failing to persist their cursor — the latter is a client bug that also burns bandwidth.

panels.title: Overdue approvals
panels.description: Before assuming inattentive managers, check notification delivery for that tenant — a broken push token looks exactly the same from here.

panels.title: Notification delivery
panels.description: A failure rate above 20% is usually an expired FCM or APNs credential. Approvals silently stop reaching people, which presents as a workflow problem rather than an infrastructure one.
